slides.0.title: Roussillon dry wines
slides.0.subtitle: Côtes du Roussillon, Collioure and Côtes Catalanes
slides.1.title: The face of Roussillon
slides.1.highlights.0.title: Spanish in character
slides.1.highlights.0.content: Jancis Robinson calls the climate "almost Spanish" and says Collioure "speaks Spanish rather than French"; the culture is Catalan
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Terrain
slides.1.highlights.1.content: Narrow valleys and terraces at the Pyrenean edge; schist soils appear in the upper Agly Valley, home to ancient vines
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Proportion
slides.1.highlights.2.content: Roussillon is about a tenth of combined output but about 80% of France's VDN (Wine With Seth)
slides.1.content: Roussillon runs three tracks in parallel: red, white and sweet.
slides.2.title: The Côtes du Roussillon family
slides.2.highlights.0.title: Villages
slides.2.highlights.0.content: Côtes du Roussillon-Villages is restricted to the northern third of Roussillon (Jancis Robinson); French Entrée says it is red only with strict variety rules, covering Agly valley villages but excluding Maury and Rivesaltes
slides.2.highlights.1.title: Les Aspres
slides.2.highlights.1.content: Côtes du Roussillon Les Aspres was created for superior wines from the south (Jancis Robinson)
slides.2.highlights.2.title: Whites
slides.2.highlights.2.content: Roussanne, Rolle (Vermentino) and Marsanne make full-bodied, often oaked whites; Grenache Blanc gives body and Maccabéo floral freshness (Jancis Robinson)
slides.2.content: Some sources are dated, so village lists and percentage rules are not tested.
slides.3.title: Collioure and Côtes Catalanes
slides.3.highlights.0.title: Same land as Banyuls
slides.3.highlights.0.content: Collioure and Banyuls share the same boundaries across four communes, Banyuls, Cerbère, Collioure and Port-Vendres, and producers may split grapes between them each season (French Entrée, Wikipedia)
slides.3.highlights.1.title: Varieties
slides.3.highlights.1.content: Mainly Grenache, Syrah and Mourvèdre with a little Carignan and Cinsaut; mostly red with some white and rosé (French Entrée)
slides.3.highlights.2.title: IGP Côtes Catalanes
slides.3.highlights.2.content: The upper Agly Valley has no appellation of its own, so many fine wines are labelled IGP Côtes Catalanes (Jancis Robinson)
slides.3.content: Sources do not state the Collioure AOC year, so none is used here.
slides.4.title: Maury Sec
slides.4.highlights.0.title: Black schist
slides.4.highlights.0.content: Maury is an almost homogeneous tract of black schist (French Entrée); Wikipedia adds more granite near Lesquerde and clay-limestone near Tautavel
slides.4.highlights.1.title: The 2011 vintage
slides.4.highlights.1.content: From the 2011 vintage Maury Sec allows dry table wines from the same varieties; before that such wines could be sold as Côtes du Roussillon-Villages (Wikipedia)
slides.4.highlights.2.title: Dated sources
slides.4.highlights.2.content: The French Entrée article dates from 2005 and a 2010 note says rules were under review, so detailed rules should be checked against official texts
slides.4.content: Maury Sec is the new entry point for dry wines in a VDN zone.
